name: RAGatouille
description: Easily use and train state of the art late-interaction retrieval methods (ColBERT) in any RAG pipeline. Designed for modularity and ease-of-use, backed by research.
editorialSummary: RAGatouille wraps ColBERT late-interaction retrieval so teams can drop research-grade reranking/retrieval into existing RAG stacks. It focuses on training and serving ColBERT indexes with a simple API.
whyCare: When dense embedding search is not enough, ColBERT via RAGatouille often lifts answer quality with relatively little pipeline churn.
notes: Last push observed mid-2025; still widely referenced for ColBERT-in-RAG. Activity verification 2026-08-12: maintenance slow→stale (pushedAt=2025-05-17T12:45:38Z, primary_status=stale).

name: Haystack
description: Open-source AI orchestration framework for building context-engineered, production-ready LLM applications. Design modular pipelines and agent workflows with explicit control over retrieval, routing, memory, and generation. Built for scalable agents, RAG, multimodal applications, semantic search, and conversational systems.
editorialSummary: Haystack is a production-oriented pipeline framework for RAG, semantic search, and agent workflows with explicit component graphs. deepset designed it for controllable retrieval, routing, and evaluation rather than opaque chains.
whyCare: Choose Haystack when you need modular, inspectable RAG/agent pipelines with strong IR roots and enterprise deployment patterns.

name: RAGFlow
description: RAGFlow is a leading open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine that fuses cutting-edge RAG with Agent capabilities to create a superior context layer for LLMs
editorialSummary: End-to-end open RAG engine with deep document understanding (DeepDoc), hybrid retrieval, and a product UI. Distinct from library stacks (LlamaIndex/Haystack) and from other self-hosted knowledge apps.
whyCare: Deploy RAGFlow when you want a self-hosted RAG product with strong document parsing—not just a Python retrieval library.
notes: GitHub primary language may report Go for some services; core product docs emphasize Python stack. Cloud/enterprise add-ons exist; Apache-2.0 covers the open core.

name: Vane
description: Vane is an AI-powered answering engine.
editorialSummary: Self-hosted AI answering/search engine (formerly Perplexica) built around local or remote LLMs plus search backends like SearXNG. Privacy-oriented alternative to cloud answer engines.
whyCare: If your “local AI stack” needs web-grounded Q&A—not just chat—this is the go-to OSS Perplexity-style stack.
notes: Renamed from Perplexica (ItzCrazyKns/Perplexica → ItzCrazyKns/Vane). localOfflineCapable false because search grounding typically needs network/SearXNG. Activity verification 2026-08-12: maintenance moderate→slow (pushedAt=2026-04-11T14:33:06Z, primary_status=low_activity). Category verification 2026-08-12: local-ai/['rag'] → rag/['local-ai'].

name: LangChain
editorialSummary: LangChain remains the most widely adopted LLM application framework, with first-class RAG primitives (retrievers, document loaders, vector store integrations) alongside agent tooling. Listed here for its retrieval ecosystem even as the project positions itself around agent engineering.
whyCare: Its retriever/vector-store ecosystem and tutorials make it the default starting point for many RAG prototypes and production apps.
notes: Primary product messaging is agent-centric; included for RAG-centric integrations and retriever abstractions.

name: GraphRAG
description: A modular graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system
editorialSummary: Microsoft Research’s modular graph-based RAG system—extracts knowledge graphs from corpora and answers with community summaries and graph traversal. Influential alternative to pure vector RAG for global sense-making questions.
whyCare: Choose GraphRAG when corpus-level themes and entity relationships matter more than nearest-neighbor chunk lookup alone.

name: txtai
description: 💡 All-in-one AI framework for semantic search, LLM orchestration and language model workflows
editorialSummary: txtai is an all-in-one embeddings + semantic search + RAG workflow library with a built-in vector index. It targets teams that want embeddings, retrieval, and LLM pipelines without assembling many separate services.
whyCare: Great fit for compact semantic-search and RAG apps where an embedded vector index plus orchestration in one package reduces stack complexity.

name: Onyx
description: Open Source AI Platform - AI Chat with advanced features that works with every LLM
editorialSummary: Onyx (formerly Danswer) is a self-hosted enterprise search and AI chat platform with connectors into workplace knowledge sources. It emphasizes permission-aware retrieval and production chat UX over raw library APIs.
whyCare: The strongest open-source option for company-internal RAG: connectors, ACL-aware search, and a full chat product you can self-host.
notes: Formerly danswer-ai/danswer; GitHub license SPDX unresolved (NOASSERTION).

name: Quivr
description: Opiniated RAG for integrating GenAI in your apps 🧠   Focus on your product rather than the RAG. Easy integration in existing products with customisation!  Any LLM: GPT4, Groq, Llama. Any Vectorstore: PGVector, Faiss. Any Files. Anyway you want.
editorialSummary: Quivr provides an opinionated RAG stack (APIs, UI patterns, vector store choices) aimed at product teams embedding knowledge chat into apps. It abstracts LLM and vector-store selection behind a product-oriented interface.
whyCare: Useful when you want a ready-made RAG product layer instead of assembling loaders, stores, and chat UI from scratch.
notes: GitHub license SPDX unresolved (NOASSERTION); activity slowed after mid-2025. Activity verification 2026-08-12: maintenance slow→stale (pushedAt=2025-07-09T12:55:23Z, primary_status=stale).

name: LlamaIndex
description: LlamaIndex is the leading document agent and OCR platform
editorialSummary: LlamaIndex is a widely used Python framework for building agentic LLM applications over private data—indexing, retrieval/query engines, connectors, and agent workflows. Retrieval-centric abstractions remain a core strength alongside broader agent tooling.
whyCare: If you are building document Q&A, knowledge agents, or multi-source RAG/agent pipelines in Python, LlamaIndex offers deep data-connection abstractions and a large integration ecosystem.

name: DSPy
description: DSPy: The framework for programming—not prompting—language models
editorialSummary: DSPy treats LM pipelines as programs with signatures, modules, and automatic optimizers instead of hand-tuned prompts. Foundational for systematic RAG/agent tuning beyond ad-hoc prompt engineering.
whyCare: Reach for DSPy when you want optimizable LM programs rather than brittle prompt strings.

name: PrivateGPT
description: Complete API layer for private AI applications on local models: RAG, skills, tools, MCP, text-to-sql, and more. Works with any OpenAI-compatible inference server.
editorialSummary: PrivateGPT is an open-source API layer that turns local (or OpenAI-compatible) models into private AI applications—document RAG and higher-level building blocks with a Claude-style API. It popularized private document Q&A and continues to emphasize on-prem/privacy-first defaults.
whyCare: Ideal when documents must stay on-prem and you want a ready API for private RAG and related app primitives rather than wiring inference and retrieval yourself.
